name: Northwest Orient (red tail)
description: Northwest Orient's scheme of the 1970s and 80s: a white upper fuselage with a straight navy band through the cabin windows from just behind door 1 all the way to the tail, bare metal below the band from nose to tail, and a plain red fin. 'NORTHWEST ORIENT' in red capitals stands just above the band from door 1, the red and white NW roundel after it on both sides. Bare metal wings and engines. Worn by its 727s, DC-10s, 747s and, from 1985, 757s ('Orient' dropped from the titles from 1986).

notes: Re-measured 2026-11-25 for ghost flights' 1985 broadcast, each type on its own measured shape: the 757 (the scheme's own paint), the passenger 727, the DC-10 and the 747 (B744-passenger standing in for the -100 and -200). The band is a level stripe: its edges are level lines in meters with a point at every crown and belly point of the shape, held within 0.3 mm of level, so it runs straight from its square front end just behind door 1 to the tail cone, where the belly's sweep or the tail's end takes it. The bare metal's top is the band's lower edge carried level forward to the nose. Heights were read against the cabin windows (the band's top is at or just above their tops on every type) and places between the doors. The crown is white: side-on photos show a grey-blue strip along it, the sky reflected at a grazing angle, but photos from above show it white. For Skyarium's ghost flights: a past scheme of a past airline.

B722-passenger.note: On the 727-200 the band is 0.77 m tall, level from the windows' tops (0.77 m over the centerline) down to the centerline, with bare metal under it. On the left it starts just behind door 1 (5.6 m back), on the right just behind the right-hand forward door (7.3 m), so the title, about 7.1 m long with capitals 0.42 m tall 0.17 m over the band, starts there on each side and the roundel follows it. The band runs on under the side engines to the tail cone, as photos show it between and behind the nacelles. Measured on N285US (left, June 1984) and N207US (right, June 1984).

DC10.note: On the DC-10 the band is 1.4 m tall, from just over the windows' tops (0.85 m over the centerline) to 0.55 m under it, square at its front 0.45 m behind door 1 and level to the tail cone under the tail engine. The title runs from just behind door 1 to past door 2 (5.8-20 m back), its capitals 0.74 m tall with their foot 0.37 m above the band, the roundel (0.82 m) at 21.5 m. Measured on N155US (left side, September 1985), the title and roundel checked on N145US (right side, 1988). The DC-10-40's JT9D nacelles aren't the CF6-50s the DC10 shape draws.

B742.note: On the 747-100 and -200 (shapes/B742.json; measured on the 747-400's shape, whose main deck is the same) the band is 1.28 m tall, from just over the main deck windows' tops (0.33 m over the centerline) to 0.95 m under it, square at its front just behind door 1 (10.2 m back) and level until the belly's sweep up to the tail takes it; the tail cone above it is white. One title, 'NORTHWEST ORIENT' 17 m long with capitals about 1 m tall, stands 0.37 m above the band from just behind door 1 to short of the wing, well under the upper deck's windows; the roundel, 1.3 m across, follows it at 28.7 m. A small US flag is high on the fin near its leading edge. Measured on N604US (left, May 1987) and checked on it from the right (June 1983) and on a 747-200 (September 1984).
